title: A tiled matrix multiply
show: lambda c: ' '.join('%.17g' % v for r in c for v in r)
starter:
def matmul_tiled(a: list[list[float]], b: list[list[float]], th: int, tw: int) -> list[list[float]]:
    n, p, m = len(a), len(b), len(b[0])
    c = [[0.0] * m for _ in range(n)]
    return c
hints: Five loops, outermost first: tile row `ib`, tile column `jb`, then `k`, then the rows `i` and columns `j` inside the tile.
Tile `(ib, jb)` covers rows `ib*th` to `ib*th + th - 1` and columns `jb*tw` to `jb*tw + tw - 1`.

The innermost line is the same as in the plain loops: add `a[i][k] * b[k][j]` onto `c[i][j]`. Because `k` counts up outside the two in-tile loops, every sum still gets its terms in the order `k = 0, 1, 2, ...`.
explain: The tile loops `ib` and `jb` pick a block of outputs. For each `k`, the two inner loops add one more term to every sum in the block. Each `c[i][j]` still receives its products in the order `k = 0, 1, 2, ...`, one add at a time, so the floats match the plain triple loop bit for bit. Only the order in which different outputs take their turns has changed.
